name: Receipt arithmetic
definition: For each number x in readings, multiply x by 2, then add 3. Put each answer in the result list. Keep the original order. For example, 4 becomes 11, and -2 becomes -1.
intro: For each number x in readings, multiply x by 2, then add 3. Put each answer in the result list. Keep the original order. For example, 4 becomes 11, and -2 becomes -1. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Stamp gates
definition: Read readings from left to right. Change each number below 0 to 0. Keep every other number as it is. Put the numbers in the result list in the same order.
intro: Read readings from left to right. Change each number below 0 to 0. Keep every other number as it is. Put the numbers in the result list in the same order. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Ribbon totals
definition: Start a total at 0. Read readings from left to right. Add each number to the total, then put the new total in the result list. For [2, 3, -1], the result list is [2, 5, 4].
intro: Start a total at 0. Read readings from left to right. Add each number to the total, then put the new total in the result list. For [2, 3, -1], the result list is [2, 5, 4]. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Reset tallies
definition: Start a total at 0. Read readings from left to right. If the next number is 0, reset the total to 0. Otherwise, add that number to the total. Put the total in the result list after each number.
intro: Start a total at 0. Read readings from left to right. If the next number is 0, reset the total to 0. Otherwise, add that number to the total. Put the total in the result list after each number. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Digit workshop
definition: Find the digit sum of each number in readings. Ignore a minus sign, then add the digits. For example, -305 gives 3 + 0 + 5 = 8. The digit sum of 0 is 0. Keep the answers in input order.
intro: Find the digit sum of each number in readings. Ignore a minus sign, then add the digits. For example, -305 gives 3 + 0 + 5 = 8. The digit sum of 0 is 0. Keep the answers in input order. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Neighbor notes
definition: Start at the second number in readings. Subtract the number just before it from the current number. Repeat for each later number. Put the answers in order. For [5, 8, 2], the result list is [3, -6]. A list with fewer than two numbers gives an empty result list.
intro: Start at the second number in readings. Subtract the number just before it from the current number. Repeat for each later number. Put the answers in order. For [5, 8, 2], the result list is [3, -6]. A list with fewer than two numbers gives an empty result list. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Ribbon runs
definition: A run is a group of matching characters next to each other. End a run only when the character changes or the text ends. Record the length of each run, from left to right. Spaces count as characters too. For "aa bb", the result list is [2, 1, 2].
intro: A run is a group of matching characters next to each other. End a run only when the character changes or the text ends. Record the length of each run, from left to right. Spaces count as characters too. For "aa bb", the result list is [2, 1, 2]. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Positive trays
definition: Keep only numbers greater than 0 from readings. Put them in the result list in their original order. Keep repeated numbers. Leave out 0 and negative numbers.

Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Drawer grids
definition: drawers is a list of rows. Add the numbers in each row. Put one total per row in the result list, in row order. An empty row has a total of 0.
intro: drawers is a list of rows. Add the numbers in each row. Put one total per row in the result list, in row order. An empty row has a total of 0. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Word slips
definition: Read line from left to right. Here, a word is a group of characters with no spaces inside it. Record the length of each word. Ignore extra spaces before, after, or between words. For "a  cat", the result list is [1, 3].
intro: Read line from left to right. Here, a word is a group of characters with no spaces inside it. Record the length of each word. Ignore extra spaces before, after, or between words. name: Frequency files
definition: Count how many times each different number appears in readings. Sort the different numbers from smallest to largest. Put their counts in that order in the result list. For [5, 2, 5], the numbers are 2 and 5, so the result list is [1, 2].
intro: Count how many times each different number appears in readings. Sort the different numbers from smallest to largest. Put their counts in that order in the result list. name: First arrivals
definition: Keep the first copy of each number in readings. Skip any later copies of the same number. Keep the order in which the numbers first appear. For [4, 2, 4, 3, 2], the result list is [4, 2, 3].
intro: Keep the first copy of each number in readings. Skip any later copies of the same number. Keep the order in which the numbers first appear. For [4, 2, 4, 3, 2], the result list is [4, 2, 3]. name: Shared drawers
definition: drawers contains two lists of numbers. Find the numbers that appear in both lists. Put each matching number in the result list only once. Sort the result list from smallest to largest.
intro: drawers contains two lists of numbers. Find the numbers that appear in both lists. Put each matching number in the result list only once. Sort the result list from smallest to largest. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Remainder boxes
definition: There are five boxes, numbered 0 to 4. For each number x in readings, find its box with ((x % 5) + 5) % 5. The % symbol means remainder. This formula also gives a box for negative numbers: -1 goes in box 4. Count the numbers in each box. The result list must contain five counts, in box order 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

name: Magnitude order
definition: Sort readings by distance from 0, from nearest to farthest. This distance is called absolute value: both -4 and 4 have distance 4. When two numbers have the same distance, put the smaller number first. Keep all repeated numbers. For [3, -2, 2, -3], the result list is [-2, 2, -3, 3].

When two numbers have the same distance, put the smaller number first. Keep all repeated numbers. For [3, -2, 2, -3], the result list is [-2, 2, -3, 3]. name: Facing cards
definition: readings is already sorted from smallest to largest. Pair its first and last numbers, then its second and second-last numbers. Keep moving toward the middle. Add the two numbers in each pair and record that sum. If one middle number is left, record it by itself. Keep this pair order in the result list.

name: Duplicate carriage
definition: readings is already sorted from smallest to largest. Keep only one copy of each number. Put these numbers in the result list in sorted order.

name: Fixed panels
definition: A window is a group of numbers next to each other. Take each window of exactly k numbers in readings, moving one place right each time. Record each window sum from left to right. If the whole input has fewer than k numbers, the result list is empty.
intro: A window is a group of numbers next to each other. Take each window of exactly k numbers in readings, moving one place right each time. Record each window sum from left to right. name: Expanding panels
definition: All numbers in readings are 0 or greater. For each position, find the shortest group that ends at that position and has a sum of at least k. The group must contain at least one number, and its numbers must be next to each other. Record the length of that group. Record 0 if no such group exists. Put one answer per position in the result list.

The group must contain at least one number, and its numbers must be next to each other. Record the length of that group. Record 0 if no such group exists. Put one answer per position in the result list. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Prefix stencils
definition: For each position in readings, add the current number and up to k - 1 numbers just before it. Stop at the start of the input if needed. Record each sum, from left to right. For readings = [2, 3, 4] and k = 2, the result list is [2, 5, 7].

The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Paired drawers
definition: drawers contains two lists, each already sorted from smallest to largest. Combine their numbers into one sorted result list. Keep all repeated numbers, including copies from both input lists.
intro: drawers contains two lists, each already sorted from smallest to largest. Combine their numbers into one sorted result list. Keep all repeated numbers, including copies from both input lists. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Canceling stamps
definition: Treat readings as a row of stamps. Keep a stack, which is a pile where you can add or remove only the top stamp. Read the stamps from left to right. If the next stamp matches the top stamp, remove the top stamp and do not add the new one. Otherwise, put the new stamp on top. The result list is the final stack, from bottom to top.

If the next stamp matches the top stamp, remove the top stamp and do not add the new one. Otherwise, put the new stamp on top. The result list is the final stack, from bottom to top. name: Taller keycaps
definition: For each number in readings, look to its right. Find the first number that is larger, not equal. Record how many places to the right it is. Record 0 if no larger number is found. Keep the answers in input order.
intro: For each number in readings, look to its right. Find the first number that is larger, not equal. Record how many places to the right it is. Record 0 if no larger number is found. Keep the answers in input order. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Round desk
definition: Each number in readings is the work time needed by a job. All jobs are ready at time 0, in input order. The worker gives the first job up to k time units. If it still needs work, put it at the back of the line. Then serve the next job. Record when each job finishes, measured from time 0. Return these finish times in original job order. A job needing 0 time finishes at time 0 and uses no worker time.

name: Window pegs
definition: Take every group of exactly k numbers next to each other in readings. Move the group one place right each time. Record the largest number in each group, from left to right. If k is larger than the input length, the result list is empty.
intro: Take every group of exactly k numbers next to each other in readings. Move the group one place right each time. Record the largest number in each group, from left to right. If k is larger than the input length, the result list is empty. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. name: Undo drawer
definition: Use a stack, which is a pile where you add and remove items only at the top. Read readings from left to right. A number of 0 or more adds that number to the top. A negative number tells you how many top items to remove: -3 means remove up to three items. Stop if the stack becomes empty. The result list is the final stack, from bottom to top.
intro: Use a stack, which is a pile where you add and remove items only at the top. Read readings from left to right. A number of 0 or more adds that number to the top. A negative number tells you how many top items to remove: -3 means remove up to three items. Stop if the stack becomes empty. The result list is the final stack, from bottom to top. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Recursive shelves
definition: Start with the whole readings list as a section. Record the sum of that section. If it has more than one number, split it into a left half and a right half. Use the same steps on the left half first, then on the right half. When a section has an odd length, the left half has one fewer number. A section with one number is not split. Do not record empty sections. The result list contains the sums in the order you record them.

Use the same steps on the left half first, then on the right half. When a section has an odd length, the left half has one fewer number. A section with one number is not split. name: Sorting press
definition: Sort readings from smallest to largest using merge sort. To use merge sort, split the list into smaller parts, sort those parts, then join the sorted parts in order. Keep all repeated numbers. The result list is the sorted list.
intro: Sort readings from smallest to largest using merge sort. To use merge sort, split the list into smaller parts, sort those parts, then join the sorted parts in order. Keep all repeated numbers. The result list is the sorted list. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Insertion tabs
definition: drawers contains two rows: a sorted number list, then a list of queries. Each query is a number to look up. For each query, find the first position in the sorted list whose number is at least the query. Positions, also called indexes, start at 0. If no number is large enough, record the length of the sorted list. Put the answers in query order.

For each query, find the first position in the sorted list whose number is at least the query. Positions, also called indexes, start at 0. name: Square gauges
definition: For each number x in readings, find the largest whole number r whose square is at most x. A square means a number multiplied by itself. For example, x = 10 gives 3, because 3 * 3 = 9 but 4 * 4 = 16. Use whole-number comparisons, not rounded decimal square roots. Keep the answers in input order.

name: Bit ribbons
definition: Write each number in readings in binary, the number system that uses only 0 and 1. Count the 1s in that form. For example, 5 is 101 in binary, so its count is 2. The count for 0 is 0. Put the counts in input order.

name: Xor register
definition: Start a stored number at 0. Read readings from left to right. Combine the stored number and the next number with bitwise XOR. XOR compares their binary digits: matching digits give 0, and different digits give 1. Use leading zeros when needed. For example, 3 XOR 5 is 6 because 011 XOR 101 gives 110. Record the stored number after each update.

name: Chain inspection
definition: head is the first node of a linked list. A node holds a number in val and a link to the next node in next. Follow next until there are no more nodes. Record each val in order. The list has no loops. An empty list gives an empty result list.

name: Chain turntable
definition: Reverse the links in the linked list given by head. Each node has a number in val and a link in next. After the links are reversed, follow the new list from start to end. Record its values in that order. An empty list gives an empty result list.

name: Midpoint chain
definition: Find the middle node of the linked list given by head. Each node stores a number in val and a link in next. Use two pointers: one moves one link at a time, and the other moves two. If there are two middle nodes, choose the second one. Record the values from that middle node to the end. An empty list gives an empty result list.

If there are two middle nodes, choose the second one. Record the values from that middle node to the end. An empty list gives an empty result list. Each card builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.

name: Branch notebook
definition: A binary tree is a set of nodes, each with a value and up to two children: left and right. root is the top node. Visit a node by recording its value, then visit its whole left branch, then its whole right branch. Use this same rule at every node. Skip missing children. The result list is the recorded values. An empty tree gives an empty result list.

Visit a node by recording its value, then visit its whole left branch, then its whole right branch. Use this same rule at every node. Skip missing children. The result list is the recorded values. name: Floor register
definition: root is the top node of a binary tree. Each node has a value and up to two children. The root is at depth 0, its children are at depth 1, and so on. Add the values at each depth. Put one sum per depth in the result list, starting at depth 0. Missing children add nothing. An empty tree gives an empty result list.

name: Catalog branches
definition: root is a binary search tree with no repeated values. In this tree, all values in a left branch are smaller than its parent, and all values in a right branch are larger. Find values from k through k + 12, including both ends. Put them in the result list from smallest to largest. Skip branches whose values cannot be in this range. An empty tree gives an empty result list.

name: Switchboard rings
definition: A graph is a set of points joined by paths. Here, paths go in one direction. Start at point 0. For each point, find the fewest paths you must follow to reach it. Record these distances in point order: 0, 1, 2, and so on. The distance to point 0 is 0. Record -1 for a point you cannot reach. A graph with no points gives an empty result list.

name: Dispatch order
definition: Each point in this graph is a task. A path from task a to task b means a must happen before b. Put all tasks with no paths coming into them in a queue, in number order. A queue serves the task at its front first. Remove that task, record its number, and remove its outgoing paths. Check its next tasks in number order. Add a task to the back of the queue as soon as it has no paths left coming in. If you cannot record every task, the rules contain a loop: use an empty result list instead.

name: Weighted lines
definition: Each point in this graph is a place, and each one-way path has a travel cost. Start at point 0. Find the lowest total travel cost to each point. Put these costs in point order. The cost to point 0 is 0. Record -1 for any point you cannot reach. A graph with no points gives an empty result list.

name: Priority basket
definition: Put all numbers from readings into a min-heap. A min-heap is a tree-shaped collection that keeps its smallest number at the top. Remove the smallest number, record it, and repeat until the heap is empty. Keep repeated numbers. The result list is the removal order.

name: Cable families
definition: This graph has two-way links between points. Points belong to the same group if you can travel between them, even through other points. Use union-find: start with one group per point, then join groups when a link connects them. For each point, count all points in its group, including itself. Record these counts in point order. A link from a point to itself does not make a larger group. A graph with no points gives an empty result list.

name: Prefix cabinet
definition: A prefix is the start of a word. For example, "c", "ca", and "cat" are the prefixes with at least one letter of "cat". For each word in words, look at all its prefixes with at least one letter. Count how many input words start with each prefix, then add those counts. Count repeated input words separately, and include the word itself. Put one total per word in the result list, in input order.

name: Island ledgers
definition: This graph has two-way links between points. A group, also called a connected component, contains all points that can reach one another. Start at point 0, then check the other points in number order. Whenever a point has not been visited, explore its whole group depth first: follow a path as far as you can before going back. Record how many points are in that group. The result list follows the order in which you first find the groups. A graph with no points gives an empty result list.
